title.narrative: Strengthening Land Governance for Sustainable Development in Ethiopia

description.narrative: Aligned with the Global Gateway priorities, namely ¿Climate & Energy¿ and ¿Digital¿. This Action strengthens land governance as a foundation for climate action and sustainable land use, land management, tenure security, responsible infrastructural investments in agriculture, digital services for land administration, contributing to Ethiopia¿s environmental and socio-economic resilience, and contributing to protect and promote European investments in agribusiness. The Action addresses critical challenges in Ethiopia¿s land governance, including:·High greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from land use: the AFOLU sector contributes 85% of total emissions (MtCO2eq), driven by deforestation, land degradation, and poor land management practices. ·Tenure insecurity: weak land administration and incomplete guarantees of land rights reduce incentives for sustainable practices and investments.·Challenges in pastoral areas: customary institutions dominate, statutory laws barely reflect the pastoral context and thus are weakly enforced , and vulnerable groups, including women, face increased marginalization. ·Uncoordinated land use: lack of land use policy and planning has led to significant land degradation (deforestation, soil erosion) dwindling of surface and underground hydrology, reduced agricultural productivity, high land fragmentation and food insecurity. ·Institutional challenges: overlapping and fragmented mandates, and poor institutional collaboration exacerbate inefficiencies and worsen resource degradation. Institutional set ups, capacities and frameworks are weak and deficient. The governmental authorities are unable to fulfil their respective mandate and enforce law.·Impacts on ecosystems and livelihoods: decreasing forest, bush encroachment, degraded shrubland and grasslands have negatively affected ecosystems and rural livelihoods, .exharcerbated by the effects of climate change The Action¿s first specific objective aims to address trade-offs between different land uses, such as agriculture, conservation, and other activities like climate mitigation, by establishing inclusive, integrated land use planning. This will be achieved through formulating and digitizing policies, developing sustainable climate-resilient land use frameworks adopting territorial approaches, strengthening institutional capacities, and fostering participatory processes. The second specific objective targets systematic land registration and certification to enhance tenure security and promote sustainable land investments. Together, these objectives address governance gaps, reduce emissions, improve resilient rural livelihoods, and foster sustainable agriculture, contributing to SDGs 1, 2, 5, 13, and 15. By addressing tenure security and facilitating participatory and integrated land use planning (i.e. tenure-responsive land use planning), and land management, the Action creates the conditions necessary for sustainable agricultural practices, rural development, and infrastructure investments. This complements the EU Action (AAP 2024 part two) Green Business Development for Sustainable Agri-Food Systems in Ethiopia by establishing robust land governance systems as a prerequisite for sustainable agri-food systems.
